core_relation.sentence: The resurrection conclusion rests on a set of minimal historical facts (crucifixion, burial, appearances, transformation, early proclamation, skeptic conversions) that are individually conceded by critical scholars and jointly require a resurrection explanation, since no naturalistic theory can account for all of them.
core_relation.quote: And I argued that I'm going to use two kinds of facts. Number one is by far the most important criterion. Number one, I will use no data that are not strongly evidenced by many other pieces of data. This is not the same as multiple attestation of texts, but you could call it multiple attestation of arguments. Every fact I use will have many facts coming in. [S348][S349][S350]

product_test.quote: If you take this approved list, you can refute you can give the major reputations of every naturalistic theory. [S647]
product_test.reason: Habermas treats the six minimal facts as a cumulative set whose explanatory power collapses if any one is removed — e.g., without the disciples' willingness to die, the stolen-body theory revives (S372–S373); without the early proclamation, the legend-development theory revives. The argument is a conjunction, not a disjunction.

slots.plays_role: External negentropy influx: the resurrection itself as an outside action of God breaking into the closed system of history, and the early creedal tradition as an external source of coherence that Paul receives rather than invents.
slots.quote: If he's raised from the dead, dead men can't raise themselves. So the father would have according to Jesus, the father acted on him. [S469][S470]

slots.plays_role: Alignment: the disciples' willingness to die and Paul's transformation show coupling between belief and life-orientation; the 'I do' of salvation as alignment with the factual data.
slots.quote: If you're willing to do that over and over again, then you are willing to die because you put yourself in that position. [S441]

slots.plays_role: Signal fidelity: the criteria of authenticity (eyewitness, early, embarrassment, enemy attestation, Aramaic substrata) are explicitly tests for whether the historical signal survives transmission through the noise of oral tradition and later redaction.
slots.quote: Is the text written by an eyewitness? ... Is it early? ... What about embarrassment? [S013][S015][S023]

slots.plays_role: Effective entropy: naturalistic theories (stolen body, legend, hallucination, Elvis/Superman parodies) function as the noise that lowers explanatory coherence; the minimal facts are chosen precisely because they resist this entropy.
slots.quote: Most critics today have given up naturalistic theories. [S649]

slots.plays_role: Temporal integration: the entire argument is a timeline — cross, conversion of Paul, pre-Pauline creeds, 1 Thessalonians, the Gospels — and the closeness of the creeds to the events is what makes the argument work.
slots.quote: These texts are they predate the books in which they're written. [S183]

slots.plays_role: Compression: the creeds and sermon summaries are compressed summaries of the gospel (deity, death, resurrection) that carry the essential meaning in a few lines; the 'one-liner' of Balkam is explicitly praised for packing a punch.
slots.quote: I love oneliners that have a pack a real punch. [S203]

slots.plays_role: Phase transition: the disciples' transformation from despair to willingness to die, and Paul's conversion from persecutor to apostle, are threshold changes of state, not gradual increments.
slots.quote: Disciples despared. They just lost their best friend. ... the disciples were transformed. [S412][S431]

slots.plays_role: Superposition: the unresolved state of competing hypotheses (naturalistic vs. resurrection) before the evidence is weighed; Habermas presents the facts as leaving the resurrection as the best explanation while critics like Crossley 'grant all six' but refuse the conclusion.
slots.quote: I'll grant all six and I'm just not in the faith. [S670]

slots.plays_role: Non-local correlation: the corporate nature of the appearances (groups, the Twelve, all the apostles) and the chain of testimony from Peter and James to Paul create a network of correlated witnesses rather than isolated reports.
slots.quote: Six. Three appearances to individuals, three appearances to groups. That's very, very important. The group appearances in particular. [S147][S148][S149][S150]

slots.plays_role: Integration: the minimal facts argument itself is the integrator — Habermas as the scholar who assembles the data into a single cumulative case, and the 'I do' of salvation as the point where the facts are integrated into a life.
slots.quote: salvation is saying I do to the factual data about Jesus. [S682]

one_line: Habermas's minimal-facts argument is a cumulative, multiplicative case for the resurrection whose criteria of authenticity map most directly onto E (signal fidelity) and T (temporal integration), with G, M, S_eff, K, R, F, and C playing analogous roles and Q only stretched.
breaks: The paper treats the empty tomb as optional (conceded by only ~75% of scholars), whereas the master equation requires all factors; Habermas explicitly brackets it out of the six minimal facts.
The role of G (external negentropy) is asserted theologically rather than demonstrated historically; the paper's method is strictly historical and cannot itself supply the outside action it needs.

The product test is applied to the facts, not to the conclusion: the facts multiply, but the inference to resurrection is presented as best explanation, which is closer to abductive reasoning than to a multiplicative product.
Q (superposition) is not genuinely unresolved in the paper's own framing — Habermas treats the resurrection as the conclusion the evidence forces, so the slot is stretched.
extra_factors: The criteria of authenticity (eyewitness, early, embarrassment, enemy attestation, Aramaic substrata) function as a meta-factor governing which data enter the product, with no direct slot.
The distinction between 'minimal facts' conceded by critics and 'maximal facts' held by believers introduces a two-tier structure not present in the master equation.
The 'I do' of salvation as a volitional response to data is an additional factor (personal commitment) that is not one of the ten slots.
